stories.title: Governors Island Issues RFEI for Revitalization of Former YMCA, Theater
stories.excerpt: The Trust for Gov­er­nors Island has released a Request for Expres­sions of Inter­est (RFEI) for the revi­tal­iza­tion of two his­toric build­ings on the Island, Build­ing 324 and Build­ing 330. The RFEI invites ideas from prospec­tive part­ners for the revi­tal­iza­tion of these his­toric assets, bring­ing them back into active, year-round use. The Trust seeks respons­es that pro­pose arts and cul­tur­al, recre­ation­al, or oth­er pub­lic-fac­ing uses. The two adja­cent build­ings are locat­ed with­in the Gov­er­nors Island His­toric Dis­trict. Orig­i­nal­ly con­struct­ed as a YMCA recre­ation cen­ter and a movie the­ater, respec­tive­ly, the build­ings fea­ture high ceil­ings and open floor plans. “The for­mer YMCA and Fort Jay The­ater his­tor­i­cal­ly stood as cul­tur­al anchors of Gov­er­nors Island, and we’re thrilled to present a unique oppor­tu­ni­ty to breathe new life into these icon­ic build­ings,” said Clare New­man, pres­i­dent and CEO of the Trust for Gov­er­nors Island. ​“We’re seek­ing vision­ary part­ners with bold ideas for cul­tur­al, recre­ation­al, and pub­lic-fac­ing uses that can turn untapped poten­tial into vibrant spaces for every­one to enjoy.” The com­plete RFEI can be viewed here. Submissions are due by Oct. 26. The post Governors Island Issues RFEI for Revitalization of Former YMCA, Theater appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trust for Governors Island seeks RFEI for two historic buildings: former YMCA and theater.
Uses limited to arts, cultural, recreational, or public-facing; submissions due October 26.
High ceilings and open floor plans in historic district; no residential multifamily permitted.
stories.summary: The Trust for Governors Island released an RFEI for revitalization of two historic buildings (Building 324, a former YMCA, and Building 330, a former movie theater) with submissions due October 26. The trust explicitly seeks arts, cultural, recreational, or public-facing uses only. The buildings feature high ceilings and open floor plans but sit within a historic district with strict use restrictions.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. The explicit constraint against residential uses and historic district protections make these assets unsuitable for apartment construction. However, any successful adaptive reuse could indirectly increase foot traffic and neighborhood vitality on Governors Island, potentially supporting future mixed-use or residential projects elsewhere on the island.

stories.title: 1031 Exchange Solutions Provider Joins Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced that Deferred, the first and only technology-powered qualified intermediary transforming 1031 exchanges for everyday real estate investors, has joined Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program as a provider of 1031 exchange solutions. The relationship is designed to provide Marcus & Millichap’s clients with streamlined access to qualified intermediary services and technology-enabled 1031 exchange solutions. As interest rates, tax considerations, and market conditions continue to influence investment decisions, many commercial real estate owners seek ways to maximize after-tax proceeds while maintaining purchasing power. Through this relationship, Marcus & Millichap’s clients will gain access to Deferred’s exchange platform, educational resources, and experienced exchange professionals. “1031 exchanges remain one of the most effective tools available to investors seeking to preserve equity and reposition capital,” said Richard Matricaria, chief growth officer of Marcus & Millichap. “Deferred provides a modern, client-focused approach to guiding investors through the exchange process. Their combination of expertise, service and technology makes them a valuable addition to our Preferred Partner Program.” The post 1031 Exchange Solutions Provider Joins Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Deferred joins Marcus & Millichap Preferred Partner Program for 1031 exchange services.
Rising interest rates and tax considerations drive investor appetite for 1031 exchanges.
Tech-enabled platform streamlines exchange process to retain capital and reposition across assets.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap partnered with Deferred, a technology-enabled qualified intermediary, to offer streamlined 1031 exchange solutions to its clients. The relationship reflects growing investor demand for 1031 exchanges as interest rates and tax implications drive decisions to preserve equity and reposition capital. Deferred provides modern platform access, education, and exchange professionals to facilitate the process.
stories.impact: Signals sustained investor appetite for portfolio repositioning and capital preservation strategies in a higher-rate environment. For multifamily developers, this indicates that 1031 exchanges remain a key liquidity tool driving asset sales and reinvestment cycles—meaning expect continued property turnover, potential acquisitions from sellers exiting higher-basis properties, and opportunity windows as capital redeploys into new developments or value-add acquisitions across markets.

stories.title: Greystone Provides $92M in Fannie Mae Loans to Metropolitan Realty
stories.excerpt: Greystone has provided a total of $91,851,000 in Fannie Mae loans to refinance and acquire three affordable housing communities located in New York. The financing was originated by senior managing director Eric Rosenstock and EVP Jeff Englund on behalf of Metropolitan Realty Group. The financing includes three affordable multifamily communities that will each undergo moderate rehabilitation as part of the transaction. Built in 1975, Pine Town Houses is a 130-unit garden-style apartment community in Long Beach, NY. Hudson View II and III, in Northern Manhattan’s Hamilton Heights neighborhood, total 129 apartments and 11 commercial spaces. Ariel Property Advisors recently arranged the Hudson View II and III acquisition. Each non-recourse, fixed-rate Fannie Mae loan features a 10-year term with five years of interest-only payments, followed by a 35-year amortization schedule. All three properties are supported by long-term Section 8 Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) contracts and are subject to long-term affordability restrictions.  The post Greystone Provides $92M in Fannie Mae Loans to Metropolitan Realty appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Greystone closed $91.85M Fannie Mae financing for Metropolitan Realty Group; three NY affordable properties.
Pine Town Houses (130 units, Long Beach); Hudson View II/III (129 units + retail, Hamilton Heights).
10-year fixed rate, five interest-only, then 35-year amortization; all backed by Section 8 HAP contracts.
stories.summary: Greystone originated $91.85 million in non-recourse Fannie Mae loans for Metropolitan Realty Group to refinance and acquire three affordable multifamily communities in New York: Pine Town Houses (130 units, Long Beach, built 1975) and Hudson View II & III (129 units, Northern Manhattan). All three properties carry long-term Section 8 Housing Assistance Payment contracts and affordability restrictions. Loans feature 10-year terms with five years interest-only followed by 35-year amortization.
stories.impact: Reflects strong Fannie Mae appetite for Section 8-backed affordable housing in Gateway markets (Long Beach, Manhattan), signaling stable capital availability for preservation and moderate rehab of rent-restricted assets. For developers, this indicates HUD/public housing finance remains accessible, but development focus is narrowing to acquisition and stabilization rather than ground-up construction in these tight, affordability-constrained submarkets.

stories.title: E Ink Breaks Ground on Expansion of Billerica Innovation Center
stories.excerpt: E Ink, an originator, pioneer and global commercial leader in ePaper technology, broke ground on the expansion of its U.S. headquarters in Billerica, MA. The project expands the footprint at the company’s Billerica Innovation Center, which is home to 260-plus E Ink employees and serves as a key global R&D center. “Expanding our Billerica campus strengthens our ability to advance technology innovation in the United States, support our customers around the world, and contribute to the continued growth of the local economy and innovation community,” said Paul Apen, chief business and operations officer at E Ink Construction is expected to be completed by March 2027 with support from NV5 Planning & Design, Inc., IF Design L.L.C., and SPEC Process Engineering & Construction, Inc.E Ink was spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 1997 and has been headquartered in Billerica since its inception. The post E Ink Breaks Ground on Expansion of Billerica Innovation Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: E Ink expands Billerica, MA headquarters and innovation center; 260+ employees anchored.
Groundbreaking underway; completion targeted March 2027.
HQ expansion strengthens U.S. R&D footprint and signals tech talent concentration in Boston metro.
stories.summary: E Ink, a pioneer in ePaper technology spun from MIT Media Lab, broke ground on an expansion of its U.S. headquarters innovation center in Billerica, Massachusetts, expected to complete by March 2027. The facility currently houses 260+ employees and serves as a global R&D hub. The expansion underscores E Ink's commitment to advancing technology innovation in the United States and supporting local economic growth.
stories.impact: Tech-sector employer expansion in Billerica/Boston metro signals job growth and talent in-migration to the Route 128 corridor. Multifamily developers should monitor: incoming senior engineers and knowledge workers will drive rental demand in East Boston, Somerville, Cambridge, and surrounding submarkets; rents will rise as young professionals relocate; this supports Class A and new-construction development near tech corridors and transit.

stories.title: Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer Provide $90M Mezz Loan for Life Science Campus
stories.excerpt: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer announced a joint investment in a $90-million mezzanine bridge loan for Aperture Del Mar, a newly constructed, 538,000-square-foot Class A life science campus in San Diego. The borrower, Gemdale USA, will use the proceeds to refinance an existing loan. The four-building lab and office campus in Del Mar Heights is fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences, a leading biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing and commercializing life-changing treatments for patients with under-addressed neurological, psychiatric, endocrine and immunological disorders. Aperture Del Mar serves as Neurocrine’s mission-critical global headquarters as part of a lease that runs through 2036. The loan is part of Breakthrough’s second life science fund, which held its first close at the end of 2025. Tishman Speyer participated through its recently established debt platform. Breakthrough is a joint venture of Tishman Speyer and Bello Capital, and has several San Diego-area properties. The post Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer Provide $90M Mezz Loan for Life Science Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer closed $90M mezzanine bridge for 538K SF life science campus.
Aperture Del Mar (Del Mar Heights, San Diego) fully leased to Neurocrine Biosciences through 2036.
Part of Breakthrough's second life science fund; Tishman Speyer debt platform participation.
stories.summary: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer jointly provided a $90 million mezzanine bridge loan for Aperture Del Mar, a newly constructed 538,000-square-foot Class A life science campus in San Diego's Del Mar Heights. The four-building campus is fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences under a long-term lease running through 2036, serving as the company's global headquarters. The loan is part of Breakthrough's second life science fund and reflects Tishman Speyer's expansion into debt.
stories.impact: Underscores continued institutional capital flow into San Diego life science real estate, driven by mission-critical tenant anchors with long-term lease stability. For multifamily developers, this signals sustained biotech/pharma job growth in San Diego, attracting highly-paid knowledge workers; prioritize rental development near biotech hubs (Sorrento Valley, Del Mar Heights) where employee in-migration and income growth will support rent appreciation and Class A fundamentals.

stories.title: West Palm Beach Multifamily Property Converted From Condos Sells for $91M
stories.excerpt: The seesaw history of a West Palm Beach residential complex has a new chapter. A joint venture between the Kamson Corporation and Joel Gluck’s Scopus Property Management has closed on a $90 million acquisition of Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, Commercial Observer has learned. The 400-unit property was built in 1990 for multifamily usage and later converted to condominiums before it was restored back to rental housing in August 2025. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl supplied an $81 million acquisition loan for the property, which encompasses 28 acres on 1401 Village Boulevard. Previous ownership consisted of individual owners of the 400 condo units who decided to terminate the communities’ condominium association last year. Meridian Capital Group negotiated the debt with a team led by David Bollag and James Darling. “Ponte Verde is a well-located community with strong bones and a clear path forward,” Bollag said in a statement. “Rather than underwriting to where the property had been, [Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl’s] teams focused on the strength and experience of the buyer and the credibility of the business plan, which allowed us to deliver a financing solution on the timeline the transaction required.” The Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes multifamily community consists of 23 two- and three-story garden-style residential buildings totaling roughly 360,488 net rentable square feet, featuring one- and two-bedroom floor plans. Community amenities include a resident clubhouse, two swimming pools, a fitness center, tennis courts, racquetball courts, a sand volleyball court, a barbecue area and spa. Prospect Ridge, Blue Owl, the Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management acquired 400-unit Ponte Verde for $90M; closed August 2025.
Property converted condo-to-rental in August 2025; built 1990, 28 acres; Prospect Ridge/Blue Owl supplied $81M debt.
Previous condo association terminated; clear path to stabilized rental operations.
stories.summary: A joint venture between Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management closed on a $90 million acquisition of Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, a 400-unit multifamily community in West Palm Beach. The property was originally built as multifamily in 1990, converted to condos, and recently restored to rental housing in August 2025 after the condo association dissolved. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl provided an $81 million acquisition loan for the 28-acre waterfront asset.
stories.impact: Signals market opportunity in condo-to-rental conversions in South Florida, where fragmented ownership and condominium association challenges create distressed inventory. For developers, this indicates: (1) pricing opportunity on condo-converted rental portfolios where exiting individual unit owners create bulk sales, (2) West Palm Beach rental market strength supporting $90M valuations on stabilized 400-unit assets, and (3) lender appetite for post-conversion refinancing at scale.

stories.title: Waste Management Buys 146-Acre Miami-Dade Development Site for $380M
stories.excerpt: Waste Management has paid nearly $380 million for about 146 acres in Medley, Fla., where the Houston-based company will likely build another landfill, property records show. The land sits parallel to Route 27 at 9515 Northwest 95th Avenue near the Everglades national park. About half the site remains vacant while the rest serves as a surface truck parking lot. The property sits adjacent to Waste Management’s 170-acre Medley Landfill complex. An entity tied to Hialeah Gardens-based Lowell Dunn Company sold the land. The same entity provided $366.8 million in seller financing, which is scheduled to mature in 2046. In a recorded easement, Lowell Dunn Company also agreed to allow Waste Management to install underground stormwater pipes across its neighboring property, enabling runoff from Waste Management’s site to discharge into a canal north of the property. Representatives for the buyer and seller did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The deal marks the second acquisition made by a waste management company in Miami-Dade County just this month. Woodlands, Texas-based Waste Connections paid $51 million for a 12-acre surface trucking parking lot in Miami Gardens. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Waste Management purchased 146 acres in Medley, FL for $380M; intended for landfill expansion.
Site near Route 27, adjacent to existing 170-acre Medley Landfill; seller financing $366.8M to 2046.
No multifamily/residential use; industrial/waste infrastructure anchors Medley submarket.
stories.summary: Waste Management paid nearly $380 million for approximately 146 acres in Medley, Florida, where the company plans to build another landfill adjacent to its existing 170-acre complex. The land, located at 9515 Northwest 95th Avenue near the Everglades, was sold by an entity tied to the Lowell Dunn Company, which also provided $366.8 million in seller financing maturing in 2046 and granted stormwater easements.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, this capital deployment signals that industrial/waste infrastructure expansion continues to concentrate in Medley (west of Miami-Dade), which may depress residential appeal and wage growth in that submarket. Multifamily developers should avoid overconcentrating Class A supply near Medley; prioritize development in Miami, Broward, and Palm Beach County submarkets with stronger employment and population in-migration.

stories.title: Carlyle Group, Haussmann Submit Plans for 99 Units at Brooklyn’s 566 Grand Avenue
stories.excerpt: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development have plans to partner on a 99-unit apartment complex in Brooklyn’s Crown Heights neighborhood. The two developers filed plans Thursday with the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) to bring a new 12-story mixed-use building to 566 Grand Avenue, near the corner of Grand Avenue and Bergen Street. Spokespeople for Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. If approved, the building will feature 99 Class A apartments, according to the filing, as well as ground-floor retail space. There will be 10 apartments on the second floor, 11 units each on the third through ninth floors, and four apartments each on floors 10, 11 and 12. The developers also plan to include several in-demand amenities at the property, such as a pet spa, a tenant theater, a game room, a children’s playroom, coworking space, a gym and an outdoor lounge. It is unclear if Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development plan to utilize the 485-x tax abatement program, which offers developers significant and lengthy tax breaks if their buildings feature a certain percentage of affordable housing. However, the 99-unit plan does provide a clue that this might be the case. A widely unpopular component of the 485-x program is higher construction wage requirements for buildings with 100 or more units. However, buildings with 99 or fewer units that utilize this program are not bound by those wage requirements. Crown Heights has been awash with residential building plans as of late. Avery Hall is planning an 18-story, 250-unit development at 1550 Bedford Avenue, while the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) is looking to build a 300-unit housing development in the neighborhood at 1119 Pacific Street. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Carlyle Group and Haussmann filed plans for 99-unit, 12-story mixed-use at 566 Grand Avenue, Crown Heights.
Class A apartments (ground-floor retail); full amenities (pet spa, theater, coworking, gym, lounge).
Crown Heights rental market tightening; potential 485-x tax abatement leverage.
stories.summary: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development filed plans with NYC Department of Buildings for a 12-story, 99-unit mixed-use building at 566 Grand Avenue in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. The building will feature Class A apartments distributed across floors (10 units floor 2, 11 each floors 3–9, four each floors 10–12) with ground-floor retail and premium amenities including pet spa, tenant theater, game room, coworking, and gym. Tax abatement program eligibility (485-x) remains under consideration.
stories.impact: Reflects aggressive Class A rental infill development in Crown Heights/Prospect Heights (a core gentrifying submarket in Brooklyn). For competitors: expect increased supply completion in 2026–2027 timeframe, which will pressure rent growth and force differentiation via amenity quality. Carlyle's entry signals investor confidence in Brooklyn rents supporting premium Class A developments; monitor lease-up timelines and achieved rents to benchmark market absorption and rental rate resilience in high-density Brooklyn neighborhoods.

stories.title: Lightstone Capital Refis San Diego Apartments With $34M Loan
stories.excerpt: Developer Jeff Svitak has landed $34.25 million of bridge debt for a newly completed San Diego multifamily project, Commercial Observer has learned. Lightstone Capital originated the senior loan for Svitak’s Kaya Apartments development in San Diego’s Bankers Hill neighborhood. John Zubak, managing director and head of origination, western region at Lightstone Capital, originated the deal. “From the outset, Kaya has been about creating housing that is deeply connected to the character of Bankers Hill while fostering a true sense of community,” Svitak said in a statement. Located at 2700 Third Avenue, Kaya Apartments debuted last year with 78 units ranging from studios to two bedrooms. Community amenities at the fully-leased complex include coworking space, community lounge, a shared kitchen and on-site café. Lightstone Capital also closed a $23.4 million senior bridge loan in July for Alliance Development Services‘ The Flats at TerraMar multifamily project in Carlsbad, Calif. Located at 5010 Avenida Encinas 32 miles north of San Diego, the 98-unit apartment community with 15 designated as affordable housing will involve converting a former Studio 6 hotel. Last but not least, Lightstone also recently originated a $11.5 million senior bridge loan for Fuller Realty‘s acquisition of an industrial property at 300 S. Sheldon Road in Channelview, Texas. bullets: Lightstone Capital originated $34.25M bridge debt for Kaya Apartments (78 units) in Bankers Hill, San Diego.
Newly completed, fully leased; studios to two-bedrooms; community amenities and on-site café.
San Diego market sustaining strong bridge lending appetite for new-construction stabilized products.
stories.summary: Developer Jeff Svitak closed a $34.25 million senior bridge loan from Lightstone Capital for Kaya Apartments, a newly completed 78-unit multifamily development in San Diego's Bankers Hill neighborhood at 2700 Third Avenue. The property is fully leased with studio to two-bedroom floor plans and community amenities. Lightstone also closed a $23.4 million bridge for Alliance Development Services' The Flats at TerraMar in Carlsbad (98 units, 32 miles north).
stories.impact: Demonstrates robust bridge lending availability for stabilized new construction in San Diego submarkets (Bankers Hill, Carlsbad). For developers: lenders remain willing to finance Class A product at completion with lease-up certainty, signaling continued capital availability. San Diego rental fundamentals remain strong enough to support bridge capital; monitor if permanent CMBS/Fannie Mae take-out rates improve to trigger refi activity and capital release for new development.

stories.title: Rexford Plans Up to $2B in Sales After Posting $507M Loss in Q2
stories.excerpt: Rexford Industrial Realty is dramatically accelerating its shift from being the most aggressive industrial buyer in Southern California into perhaps the region’s biggest seller. The Los Angeles-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has identified about $2 billion of “noncore assets” for disposition as it continues to prioritize keeping tenants in Rexford buildings. That property sales forecast is sharply up from the previous range of $400 million to $500 million. During the REIT’s earnings call Friday, CEO Laura Clark said the disposition pool encompasses about 8 million square feet with limited value-creation potential, shorter lease terms, and rents substantially above market — generally by more than 20 percent. Chief Financial Officer Michael Fitzmaurice said about $1 billion will repay debt maturing in 2027, rather than refinance into a higher rate environment. The remaining proceeds will be guided by market conditions. “We’re not de-levering to sit idle; we’re de-levering to redeploy,” Fitzmaurice said. The vast majority of Rexford’s property sales are expected to close before the end of the year. “We expect that pricing will be achieved at levels that allow us to redeploy proceeds on a neutral to accretive basis through our 2027 FFO per share, and this is not a dilutive exercise,” Clark said. Rexford said it sold seven properties totaling approximately 572,000 square feet for $137.9 million during the second quarter, after disposing of five properties for $127.4 million in the first quarter. The company previously known for 10-figure buying sprees has completed no acquisitions this year. Rexford plans to use property sales proceeds to repay debt, repurchase shares and pursue higher-yielding investments. It bought back $100 million of stock during the quarter, bringing its 2026 repurchases to $300 million, and its board subsequently authorized a new $1 billion repurchase program. bullets: Rexford Industrial accelerating dispositions to $2B (from $400–500M); identifies 8M SF 'noncore' assets.
Assets have limited value-creation potential, short lease terms, rents 20%+ above market; $1B to repay 2027 debt.
Southern California industrial cap rates rising; refinance risk driving strategic de-levering and redeployment.
stories.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty sharply increased its asset disposition guidance to approximately $2 billion (from $400–500 million previously), identifying about 8 million square feet of noncore assets with limited upside, shorter lease terms, and rents 20% above market. CEO Laura Clark stated the focus is maintaining tenant relationships, while CFO Michael Fitzmaurice noted $1 billion of proceeds will repay 2027 debt maturities rather than refinance into a higher-rate environment, with remaining capital redeployed by market conditions.
stories.impact: Signals distressed refinance dynamics in industrial real estate and rising cap-rate pressure in Southern California. Rexford's shift from buyer to seller indicates: (1) industrial valuations under pressure as cap rates widen and refinance risk looms for 2027 maturities, (2) above-market lease spreads becoming liabilities rather than assets in a higher-rate world, and (3) likely portfolio sales and asset recycling across regional markets. For multifamily developers in SoCal, monitor freed-up institutional capital—Rexford's redeployment may drive competitive bidding for land and value-add apartments.
